messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Okay, so four-motor cluster, K motors or smaller. Build me something for about 4,250 ft. Touchdown under 15 ft/s. It should handle 10 mph wind. What would you build?

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: four motors in a cluster, each at most a K. Apogee about 4,250 ft. 4250 * 0.3048 = 1300 m, so the band is 1,300 m ±5%. Touchdown at most 15 ft/s. 15 * 0.3048 = 4.6 m/s. Wind about 10 mph. 10 * 0.447 = 4.5 m/s, and that wind goes in every flight call. Rail is not stated, so I assume 1.5 m. Single stage. Vertical, sea level.
2. Feasibility: drag-free speed for 1,295 m is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 1300) = 160 m/s. Four full K motors would be far too much impulse for that altitude unless the rocket were huge. The cap is K, not a requirement to use K, so I want four smaller motors whose total impulse fits about 1,300 m. I need catalog numbers and diameters, because a 4-motor cluster has to fit inside the tube.

2. Feasibility: G80 lookup returned G80T, 135.6 N*s, 80.6 N, 29 mm. H128W is 177.8 N*s, H180W is 233.7 N*s, I200W is 326.8 N*s, all 29 mm and all under a K. Four G80T motors are 4 * 135.6 = 542 N*s. Four H128W motors are 4 * 177.8 = 711 N*s, about a third more, which is likely past 1,360 m on a light cluster rocket. I200W only lists a 0 s delay and even more impulse. I'll start with four G80T. A 29 mm mount of 0.032 m OD in a cluster of 4 needs about 0.032 * 2.4 = 0.077 m of inside width, so the tube ID has to clear that.
3. Size: guessed liftoff mass 1.3 kg. Thrust is 4 * 80.6 = 322 N, so thrust-to-weight is 322 / (1.3 * 9.81) = 25. Rail acceleration is (322 - 1.3 * 9.81) / 1.3 = 238 m/s^2 and rail exit is sqrt(2 * 238 * 1.5) = 27 m/s. Propellant is about 4 * 0.069 = 0.28 kg, descent mass 1.3 - 0.28 = 1.0 kg. Landing has to be under 4.6 m/s, so I size for 4 m/s. Area is 2 * 1.0 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 4^2) = 1.25 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 1.25 / 3.1416) = 1.3 m.
4. Draft: 86 mm blue-tube airframe, four G80T motors in one mount, four plywood fins, 1.3 m chute at apogee. Wind in the call is 4.5 m/s.

4. Check: the simulator gives apogee 1213 m. Against 1,300 m that is (1300 - 1213) / 1300 = 6.7% low, outside the 5% band, so altitude fails. Landing is 4.4 m/s, under the 4.6 m/s limit. Rail exit 28.6 m/s, thrust-to-weight 20.9, and margin 1.06 cal all pass. The margin only just clears 1.0. Liftoff mass is 1.57 kg against a 1.3 kg guess, which explains part of the shortfall. The four G80T motors are inside the K cap.
5. Fix: shorten the body from 0.75 m to 0.60 m so drag and mass both drop, without stepping up to the H motors. Fins stay put, because 1.06 cal has nothing to give away. Same four-motor mount, same 1.3 m chute, same 4.5 m/s wind.

4. Check: the simulator gives apogee 1232 m. Against 1,300 m that is (1300 - 1232) / 1300 = 5.2% low, still just outside 5%. Margin fell to 0.68 cal, under 1.0, because the shorter tube moved the CG aft. Landing is 4.2 m/s, under 4.6. Rail exit 29.0 m/s and thrust-to-weight 22.4 still pass. The length cut bought almost no altitude and broke stability.
5. Fix: step the motors up to H128W. Four of them are 711 N*s against 542 N*s from the G80T cluster, and the cases are still 29 mm, so the mount diameter stays. The H128W is 0.194 m long, so the mount grows to 0.21 m and the tube goes back to 0.72 m to hold it. Fin span goes from 0.11 m to 0.14 m so the heavier tail still clears 1 cal. Chute goes from 1.3 m to 1.4 m because the landing limit is only 4.6 m/s and the rocket got heavier. Wind stays 4.5 m/s.

4. Check: the simulator gives apogee 1288 m. Against 1,300 m that is (1300 - 1288) / 1300 = 0.9% low, inside the 5% band. Landing is 4.5 m/s, under the 4.6 m/s limit. Margin is 1.04 cal, above 1.0. Rail exit is 32.3 m/s and thrust-to-weight is 32.1. Four H128W motors are H class, inside the K cap. The chute opened, and the wind in the run was 4.5 m/s. Every check passes.
5. Fix: no further change; altitude, landing, the cluster, and the safety gates all pass.
6. Uncertainty: 1.04 cal and 4.5 m/s are both close to their limits. A heavier fin can or a chute that opens poorly can miss one of them. Chute Cd is a model 0.8. The 4.5 m/s wind will drift the rocket a long way under the 1.4 m canopy (the run shows 1169 m), which the prompt did not cap. Liftoff mass is 1.94 kg.
messages.content:
Four AeroTech H128W motors in an 86 mm blue-tube rocket, with a 1.4 m chute at apogee.
In 4.5 m/s wind the apogee is 1288 m and the landing is 4.5 m/s.
Rail exit is 32.3 m/s at 1.04 cal. The motors are under the K cap.
